case-sara.text: [Thoughtful] I'm still sad, but it doesn't feel like proof that there's something wrong with me.
case-sara.suggestion: The sadness is still here, and it no longer has to mean you're wrong. What words would help you remember that difference?

case-sara.text: [Softly] ‘I wanted company’ feels kinder than ‘I was needy’. I'm not sure I believe it yet.
case-sara.suggestion: ‘I wanted company’ feels a little kinder, even without full belief yet. What happens as you say it that way?

case-sara.text: [Pauses] I can miss him and still know I didn't feel cared for. I usually lose one of those thoughts.
case-sara.suggestion: Both can be true for you now. How would you put that in your own words, so neither part gets lost?

case-sara.text: [Uncertain] My shoulders dropped when I stopped calling myself pathetic. It'll probably be back tonight.
case-sara.suggestion: You noticed your shoulders drop, and you're wary of tonight. Could we name what helped just now, without expecting you to hold on to it perfectly?

case-sara.text: [Surprised] I said I needed him to listen, and I didn't immediately apologize. That felt different.
case-sara.suggestion: For a moment, your need could stand without an apology. What was different about letting it be there?

case-sara.text: [Quietly] I don't feel ready to date. But saying that doesn't sound like giving up anymore.
case-sara.suggestion: Not being ready feels more like knowing where you are than giving up. What would you like to take from that?

case-sara.text: [Hesitant] Maybe I can tell my friend I don't need advice, just a bit of company. That feels new.
case-sara.suggestion: You're finding words for the company you want. Would it help to try saying them here and see whether they sound like you?

case-sara.text: [Tearful] I still wish he'd come back. I just don't want to abandon myself while I wait.
case-sara.suggestion: The wish is still there, and there's also this wish to stay on your own side. What does ‘not abandon myself’ mean for you tonight?

case-sara.text: [Reflective] The anger doesn't feel mean now. It's telling me that being ignored hurt.
case-sara.suggestion: Your anger is helping you recognize the hurt instead of proving you're mean. What feels important about that change?

case-sara.text: [Half-smile] I didn't check my phone during that whole pause. I hadn't even noticed until now.
case-sara.suggestion: You noticed a pause where you weren't checking. What was occupying you instead, if anything?

case-sara.text: [Unsure] I can say I wasn't asking for too much. It feels true here, but outside this room I'm less sure.
case-sara.suggestion: It feels true here, and less certain outside. Is there a phrase from today you would want to keep nearby, without making yourself believe it on command?

case-sara.text: [Sighs] Nothing feels fixed. But I understand a little better why the evenings are hard.
case-sara.suggestion: Nothing is fixed, and the evenings make a little more sense. What have you understood that you would like us to keep hold of?

case-michael.text: [Thoughtful] Being corrected felt embarrassing. It didn’t actually make me useless.
case-michael.suggestion: What helped you separate embarrassment from being useless?

case-michael.text: [Quietly] I can say I was hurt without saying she had no right to speak.
case-michael.suggestion: What becomes clearer when you keep those two things separate?

case-michael.text: [Surprised] I admitted I didn’t know. I didn’t feel smaller afterwards.
case-michael.suggestion: What was different about not knowing in that moment?

case-michael.text: [Steady] The shouting was mine. So was the wish to be listened to.
case-michael.suggestion: How would you put both into words without using one to excuse the other?

case-michael.text: [Hesitant] Asking for a minute sounded better than ordering her to stop.
case-michael.suggestion: What did that request let you say differently?

case-michael.text: [Relieved] I let the sentence stand without proving I was right.
case-michael.suggestion: What helped you leave it without another argument?

case-michael.text: [Quietly] I’m still tense. I can hear the hurt a bit more clearly.
case-michael.suggestion: Which words capture the hurt you can hear now?

case-michael.text: [Thoughtful] I missed her before I got angry. I usually skip that bit.
case-michael.suggestion: What helps you notice that earlier moment?

case-michael.text: [Unsure] I corrected you without raising my voice. It might not work at home.
case-michael.suggestion: What made it possible here, without predicting what will happen at home?

case-michael.text: [Quietly] Dad’s voice is still there. I didn’t have to join in this time.
case-michael.suggestion: What changed in how you responded to that voice?

case-michael.text: [Moved] Wanting us to laugh again sounds different from wanting to win.
case-michael.suggestion: What do you want to keep about that difference?

case-michael.text: [Steady, cautious] I know what I regret. I don’t have to call myself a monster to own it.
case-michael.suggestion: How would you name the responsibility without that label?

case-jason.text: [Surprised] I paused, and you still waited. I didn’t have to fill it.
case-jason.suggestion: What was different about having time for your answer?

case-jason.text: [Quietly] Wanting to join them sounds less stupid here.
case-jason.suggestion: What makes that wish easier to hear here?

case-jason.text: [Hesitant] I said I didn’t understand. Nothing terrible happened.
case-jason.suggestion: What helped you say it this time?

case-jason.text: [Relieved] I can be anxious and still want the invitation.
case-jason.suggestion: How would you put those two things together in your own words?

case-jason.text: [Quietly] I stopped calling the pause a failure. It was just a pause for a moment.
case-jason.suggestion: What changed when the pause didn’t have to mean failure?

case-jason.text: [Unsure] The sentence came out. I don’t know if it’ll come out tomorrow.
case-jason.suggestion: What made it possible today, without asking tomorrow to be the same?

case-jason.text: [Thoughtful] Being left out hurt. It doesn’t prove I belong nowhere.
case-jason.suggestion: What helps you separate that painful experience from not belonging anywhere?

case-jason.text: [Warm] I remembered the part of the conversation I liked, not only the mistake.
case-jason.suggestion: What would you like to remember about the part you liked?

case-jason.text: [Hesitant] Asking for a smaller question worked better than pretending I knew.
case-jason.suggestion: What did that request give you?

case-jason.text: [Quietly] I heard how harsh I was being. I didn’t have to answer myself that way.
case-jason.suggestion: Which gentler words felt believable, even a little?

case-jason.text: [Relieved, shy] I asked you to wait. That feels like something I could ask for again.
case-jason.suggestion: Which few words would you want to keep?

case-jason.text: [Quietly] I’m still awkward. I don’t feel quite so wrong for wanting company.
case-jason.suggestion: What is different in how you hear that wish now?

case-arne.text: [Thoughtful] “I wanted company” sounds less harsh than “I’m needy.”
case-arne.suggestion: What feels different as you use those kinder words?

case-arne.text: [Softly] I can say I was tired without taking the love away.
case-arne.suggestion: How would you say that in your own words, so both the love and the tiredness have a place?

case-arne.text: [Surprised] I don’t feel guilty about that laugh for a moment.
case-arne.suggestion: Could we notice what makes room for enjoying it just now?

case-arne.text: [Steady] Missing her doesn’t mean the workshop afternoon was wrong.
case-arne.suggestion: Both can belong in your day. What would help you remember that?

case-arne.text: [Quietly] Asking Tom to stay feels more ordinary now.
case-arne.suggestion: What has changed in how you hear that request?

case-arne.text: [Softly] The tears feel like missing her, not failing.
case-arne.suggestion: “Missing her, not failing”—is that how you want to name the difference?

case-arne.text: [Thoughtful] I can keep the coat because I want to, not because I have to.
case-arne.suggestion: What is it like to feel some choice about keeping it?

case-arne.text: [Small smile] I noticed her recipe and felt warm as well as sad.
case-arne.suggestion: What feels worth keeping about having both there?

case-arne.text: [Uncertain] This is clearer here. Tonight might be different.
case-arne.suggestion: We don’t need to promise tonight. What have you understood here that you want to carry?

case-arne.text: [Reflective] I need company sometimes. That sounds reasonable when I say it now.
case-arne.suggestion: Would you like to try those words once more and hear whether they sound like you?

case-arne.text: [Sighs] Nothing is solved, but I’m less cross with myself.
case-arne.suggestion: What helped you be a little less harsh with yourself?

case-arne.text: [Quietly] I’d like to remember that rest was a need, not a betrayal.
case-arne.suggestion: Is “rest was a need” the phrase you want to take from today?

case-arne.text: [Thoughtful] I can admit the quiet was good. I still miss her in it.
case-arne.suggestion: What helps you hold those two truths together just now?

case-arne.text: [Hesitant] “Tired and loving” fits. I’m not sure Emma would understand.
case-arne.suggestion: It fits here. Could we give your wording room before deciding what to tell Emma?

case-arne.text: [Quietly] Enjoying the workshop needn’t mean leaving Eva out. That feels new.
case-arne.suggestion: What has helped enjoyment and your connection with her fit alongside each other?

case-arne.text: [Softly] The anger makes more sense. I still don’t like it.
case-arne.suggestion: Understanding it doesn’t require liking it. What have you learned about what it was asking for?

case-arne.text: [Half-smile] I asked for company without apologizing. It’ll be harder outside.
case-arne.suggestion: What was different in that request here? We can keep it small enough to recognize outside.

case-arne.text: [Uncertain] Rest isn’t betrayal. I know the words; believing them comes and goes.
case-arne.suggestion: When they fit, what do you notice? We needn’t force them to fit every time.

case-arne.text: [Quietly] I feel more entitled to choose what I keep. The coat can stay for now.
case-arne.suggestion: What is it like to make that a present choice, rather than a permanent rule?

case-arne.text: [Sighs] I’m still lonely. But needing someone doesn’t sound as embarrassing.
case-arne.suggestion: The loneliness remains; the judgment has softened a little. How would you name that difference?

case-arne.text: [Reflective] I can remember the good and the difficult parts without deciding which marriage was real.
case-arne.suggestion: What feels important about letting both belong to the same relationship?

case-arne.text: [Hesitant] “I want company, not supervision.” That’s clearer, if a bit blunt.
case-arne.suggestion: Does that wording fit you, or would you choose words that carry the same distinction more naturally?

case-arne.text: [Quietly] I don’t have to earn a good afternoon by being sad afterward.
case-arne.suggestion: What happens hearing that in your own voice?

case-arne.text: [Unsure] There’s a small change. I don’t want a homework plan attached to it.
case-arne.suggestion: We can let it be a change without a task. What, if anything, do you want to remember?

case-arne.text: [Firmly] I can name the relief. Don’t make that proof I’ve accepted her death.
case-arne.suggestion: We’ll keep it to naming the relief. What, if anything, feels different about being able to say it?

case-arne.text: [Quietly] “I loved her and was tired” fits. The guilt hasn’t agreed.
case-arne.suggestion: The words fit, while guilt remains. What do you want to keep without needing guilt’s agreement?

case-arne.text: [Watchful] I asked for company here. It doesn’t mean I can do it with Emma.
case-arne.suggestion: Here and with Emma are different. What did this request show you, without turning it into a demand for home?

case-arne.text: [Hesitant] I’m less harsh with myself. I don’t want a slogan to take home.
case-arne.suggestion: No slogan needed. Would noticing the difference quietly be enough for now?

case-arne.text: [Dryly] A small good afternoon. Not a turning point.
case-arne.suggestion: A small good afternoon. What mattered to you in that afternoon, without making it more than it was?

case-arne.text: [Quietly] I could say no without explaining everything. That’s useful, but I still feel awkward.
case-arne.suggestion: The awkwardness stays, and you noticed a choice. What part of that choice feels useful to keep?

case-arne.text: [Firmly] Understanding the anger isn’t the same as forgiving anyone.
case-arne.suggestion: We won’t equate them. What have you understood about the anger that matters on its own?

case-arne.text: [Uncertain] The words fit for a minute. Then they sounded borrowed again.
case-arne.suggestion: Could we notice what fit in that minute, and leave the borrowed-sounding part open?

case-arne.text: [Quietly] I don’t have to prove love by giving up the workshop. I still don’t know what I want next.
case-arne.suggestion: That distinction can stand without a next plan. How would you keep it in your own terms?

case-arne.text: [Watchful] I’m still sad. I just don’t feel obliged to explain it to everyone.
case-arne.suggestion: The sadness remains, with more choice about sharing it. What feels important about that choice?

case-arne.text: [Hesitant] Choosing the coat for now feels different from promising forever.
case-arne.suggestion: What does “for now” make possible for you?

case-arne.text: [Firmly] I noticed something, but I don’t want you congratulating me.
case-arne.suggestion: I won’t congratulate you. Would you like to name what you noticed, or keep it quietly your own?

case-mia.text: [Thoughtful] I can say I miss drawing without calling myself ungrateful.
case-mia.suggestion: What helped you make room for that sadness without the judgment?

case-mia.text: [Steady] “Ask me first” sounds clearer than snapping now.
case-mia.suggestion: What do you want to remember about that clearer request?

case-mia.text: [Quietly] I still need help. It doesn’t feel like I’ve disappeared when I say it now.
case-mia.suggestion: What is different in how you see yourself alongside that need?

case-mia.text: [Relieved] I can be glad Alex helps and want a say.
case-mia.suggestion: What helped those two things fit together for you?

case-mia.text: [Warmly] I noticed the part of me that still loves explaining paintings.
case-mia.suggestion: How would you like to hold onto that part, within the energy you have?

case-mia.text: [Reflective] I said I was angry, and we didn’t have to make it bigger.
case-mia.suggestion: What was helpful about giving the anger that much room?

case-mia.text: [Steady] Resting feels like responding to my limit, not failing a test.
case-mia.suggestion: What changed in how you understood the rest you needed?

case-mia.text: [Softly] The sadness is still here, but I’m less alone with it.
case-mia.suggestion: What about our conversation helped it feel less lonely?

case-mia.text: [Thoughtful] I found the words: I need help with carrying, not deciding.
case-mia.suggestion: Do those words capture what you want to keep from today?

case-mia.text: [Quietly] I noticed a good moment without using it to deny the hard ones.
case-mia.suggestion: How did you make room for that good moment alongside the hard ones?

case-mia.text: [Relieved] Stopping when I asked made it easier to say what I needed.
case-mia.suggestion: What do you want us to remember about that pace next time?

case-mia.text: [Steady] I don’t need to explain everything for my request to matter.
case-mia.suggestion: What helped you feel that your request could stand on its own?

case-mia.text: [Reflective] I found a request underneath the anger. I still don’t like how I said it.
case-mia.suggestion: What request do you want to keep, while taking responsibility for the way it came out?

case-mia.text: [Quietly] I can need Alex and still want him to wait for my answer.
case-mia.suggestion: What helped you give both the need and your answer a place?

case-mia.text: [Moved] I felt like a sister, not a list of tasks. I want to remember that.
case-mia.suggestion: What made that moment feel like being sisters?

case-mia.text: [Steady] Rest didn’t feel like giving up this time. I’m not sure that will last.
case-mia.suggestion: What was different this time, even if it isn’t something you can guarantee?

case-mia.text: [Sad, calmer] Nothing about the drawing changed. I stopped arguing with how much I miss it.
case-mia.suggestion: What helped you hear the missing without having to argue it away?

case-mia.text: [Thoughtful] I can keep the good day without making it a promise about tomorrow.
case-mia.suggestion: How would you describe that distinction in your own words?

case-mia.text: [Relieved] “Ask, then wait” is what I meant. I don’t mean never help me.
case-mia.suggestion: What do those words make clearer about the help you want?

case-mia.text: [Quietly] I’m still uncertain, but I’m less cross with myself for not knowing.
case-mia.suggestion: What softened that judgment of not knowing?

case-mia.text: [Warm, cautious] I liked offering my opinion. I don’t want that turned into a new duty.
case-mia.suggestion: What would help you keep it as something you can choose to offer?

case-mia.text: [Steady] I said stop before I was completely worn out. That felt different.
case-mia.suggestion: What helped you notice and say that limit earlier?

case-mia.text: [Reflective] The anger isn’t gone. It’s less of a blur now.
case-mia.suggestion: What has become clearer in it?

case-mia.text: [Softly] Being believed mattered more than finding the right explanation.
case-mia.suggestion: What about being believed do you want us to remember for our work?

case-mia.text: [Quietly] I found what I wanted to ask. I haven’t found a kind way to ask it yet.
case-mia.suggestion: What has become clearer in the request, even with the wording still unfinished?

case-mia.text: [Thoughtful] “Wait for my answer” fits. It doesn’t solve what happens when I don’t have one.
case-mia.suggestion: What part does that phrase capture, and what needs to remain open?

case-mia.text: [Sad, steadier] I didn’t improve the afternoon. I stopped calling myself wrong for missing it.
case-mia.suggestion: What helped you make that distinction without having to improve the loss?

case-mia.text: [Relieved, cautious] I felt believed. I’m not suddenly ready to tell everybody everything.
case-mia.suggestion: What was helpful about being believed here, at the amount you chose to share?

case-mia.text: [Warm, serious] I liked that moment at work. Please don’t turn it into evidence that I can do more.
case-mia.suggestion: We can keep it as that moment. What do you want remembered about why it mattered?

case-mia.text: [Steady] I can own the snapping without giving up the need behind it.
case-mia.suggestion: How would you put that distinction in words you could actually use?

case-mia.text: [Quietly] We stopped when I asked. That’s the thing that changed, not the feeling.
case-mia.suggestion: What difference did having your stop respected make for you?

case-mia.text: [Reflective] I need help differently on different days. I don’t have one final answer for Alex.
case-mia.suggestion: What would you want him to understand about that changing answer?

case-mia.text: [Sad, calm] I can leave the drawing out without making it a promise to finish.
case-mia.suggestion: What changed in how you let that unfinished drawing be there?

case-mia.text: [Uncertain] I don’t know if this is a change. There’s less arguing inside for a moment.
case-mia.suggestion: Could we name that small difference without deciding what it will become?

case-mia.text: [Quietly] I corrected you and you didn’t make me explain it until I was worn out.
case-mia.suggestion: What do you want us to keep about how we handled that correction?

case-mia.text: [Steady, tired] I know the words I want. Today I might only manage half of them.
case-mia.suggestion: Which few words would hold the essential part, without asking more energy from you?

case-nora.text: [Steady] I can say it hurt without having to prove I’m usually easygoing.
case-nora.suggestion: What helped you give the hurt room without that extra explanation?

case-nora.text: [Quietly] The anger has a clearer point now: I want to present my own work.
case-nora.suggestion: What do you want to keep about that clearer wish?

case-nora.text: [Relieved] “Ask me before speaking for me.” That sounds like what I mean.
case-nora.suggestion: What does that request make clearer for you?

case-nora.text: [Thoughtful] I can choose not tonight without saying never.
case-nora.suggestion: What helped those two choices feel different?

case-nora.text: [Sad, calmer] The event hasn’t changed. I’m less alone with it.
case-nora.suggestion: What helped it feel less lonely here?

case-nora.text: [Warm] I remembered that I still enjoy my work. It wasn’t a denial of what happened.
case-nora.suggestion: How do you want to hold both the enjoyment and what happened?

case-nora.text: [Steady] I don’t have to answer for everybody.
case-nora.suggestion: What changes when your own experience is enough to speak from?

case-nora.text: [Reflective] I found words for the support I want from Max.
case-nora.suggestion: Which words do you want to remember?

case-nora.text: [Relieved] I didn’t need a perfect explanation to be heard.
case-nora.suggestion: What about being heard without that explanation mattered?

case-nora.text: [Quietly] I felt the hurt without having to forgive anyone.
case-nora.suggestion: What helped you make room for your feeling on those terms?

case-nora.text: [Steady] Pausing felt like my choice, not failing to speak.
case-nora.suggestion: What made the pause feel like your choice?

case-nora.text: [Warm] The photographs were just photographs for a while. I liked that.
case-nora.suggestion: What was good about letting that pleasure be ordinary?

case-nora.text: [Thoughtful] I can love the work and object to how I was treated.
case-nora.suggestion: What helped those two things have room together?

case-nora.text: [Steady] I found a request for Max that doesn’t reject his support.
case-nora.suggestion: What do you want to keep, and what do you want changed, in that request?

case-nora.text: [Quietly] I’m uncertain about today’s interruption. Less uncertain that I deserve a hearing.
case-nora.suggestion: What made it possible to separate those two uncertainties?

case-nora.text: [Sad, calmer] I stopped arguing that it shouldn’t have hurt. It still hurts.
case-nora.suggestion: What changed when you stopped arguing with the hurt?

case-nora.text: [Relieved, cautious] Saying not tonight feels like choosing. I don’t know about tomorrow.
case-nora.suggestion: What made tonight’s choice clearer, even with tomorrow open?

case-nora.text: [Warm] I kept the ordinary evening without using it to deny the meeting.
case-nora.suggestion: How did you make room for both?

case-nora.text: [Reflective] I can regret the sharpness with Adam without taking back the hurt.
case-nora.suggestion: What words would help you keep that distinction?

case-nora.text: [Moved] Being believed made me less busy collecting evidence for a moment.
case-nora.suggestion: What was different in that moment of being believed?

case-nora.text: [Steady] I can want credit without making the firm’s response into my achievement.
case-nora.suggestion: What becomes clearer about what belongs to you and what belongs to them?

case-nora.text: [Quietly] The fear isn’t gone. It’s more specific now.
case-nora.suggestion: What has become clearer in the fear?

case-nora.text: [Thoughtful] I found a way to ask for company without another full explanation.
case-nora.suggestion: Which few words capture the company you want?

case-nora.text: [Relieved] I said stop and we stopped. It made the next choice feel more mine.
case-nora.suggestion: What do you want us to remember about respecting that stop?

case-nora.text: [Quietly] I can say what happened without softening every word. I’m not ready to tell Ben.
case-nora.suggestion: What helped the words become plainer here, without making a next step necessary?

case-nora.text: [Thoughtful] I want Max to wait for my answer. I don’t always have an answer.
case-nora.suggestion: What does that request capture, and what still needs room to remain undecided?

case-nora.text: [Sad, steadier] Nothing gave the presentation back. I stopped calling myself weak for being hurt.
case-nora.suggestion: What changed in how you treated the hurt, even with the lost opportunity unchanged?

case-nora.text: [Relieved, cautious] Being believed mattered. It doesn’t mean I want more disclosure next time.
case-nora.suggestion: What do you want us to keep about being believed at the amount you chose to share?

case-nora.text: [Warm, serious] Dinner was enjoyable. Don’t turn it into proof that I’m recovering.
case-nora.suggestion: We can keep it as that evening. What would you like remembered about why it mattered?

case-nora.text: [Steady] I can own the snapping and still stand by needing to be heard.
case-nora.suggestion: How would you put that distinction in words you could use with Adam?

case-nora.text: [Quietly] We stopped when I asked. The change was in having a choice, not in feeling better.
case-nora.suggestion: What difference did that respected choice make?

case-nora.text: [Reflective] I’m uncertain about one moment without retracting the others now.
case-nora.suggestion: What helped you give that uncertainty its own place?

case-nora.text: [Sad, calm] I can leave the drawings there without promising I’ll feel differently tomorrow.
case-nora.suggestion: What changed in how you let the unfinished moment remain?

case-nora.text: [Uncertain] I don’t know whether it’s a change. There’s less explaining inside me for a minute.
case-nora.suggestion: Could we name that small difference without deciding what it will become?

case-nora.text: [Quietly] I corrected the culture explanation. You let my own meaning stay.
case-nora.suggestion: What do you want us to remember about making room for that correction?

case-nora.text: [Steady, tired] The request is clearer. I might need fewer words when I actually use it.
case-nora.suggestion: Which few words hold the part you most want heard?
